blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Implementing logistics technology is less about software selection and more about adoption. A TMS, WMS or tracking system is only as valuable as the percentage of the team that trusts it, uses it, and lets it shape how they actually work. Everything else is marketing.

Good implementations start small: one use case, one team, one clear benefit. The team sees the benefit on day three, not day ninety. Having proven the benefit, the rollout widens. Having earned trust, the team invests in learning the harder features. Having built the habit, the system becomes part of how the operation thinks.

The worst implementations try to do everything at once — and end with expensive software nobody uses. The best ones look unambitious from the outside and transform operations quietly over a year.

items.q: According to the text, what mainly determines the value of a TMS, WMS or tracking system?
options: The price paid for the licence
The number of features it offers
The percentage of the team that trusts and uses it
items.why: "only as valuable as the percentage of the team that trusts it, uses it…" — o valor está na adoção.

items.q: How do good implementations begin?
options: With one use case, one team and one clear benefit
With a full rollout across every team
items.why: "Good implementations start small: one use case, one team, one clear benefit."

items.q: When should the team see the first benefit?
items.why: "The team sees the benefit on day three, not day ninety."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Rolling out everything at once is the safest approach.
A quick, visible win builds confidence in the system.
Adoption matters more than the software you choose.
Trust has to be earned before the rollout can widen.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que as piores implementações "try to do everything at once" — logo o autor discorda dessa ideia.

items.q: What does the phrase "look unambitious from the outside" suggest about the best implementations?
options: Their real impact is greater than their modest appearance
They avoid using any new technology
They fail to deliver lasting results
items.why: Inferência: parecem modestas, mas "transform operations quietly over a year" — o impacto supera a aparência.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily explicando como está resgatando a implementação do WMS. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, when I took this over, the WMS rollout had been stalled for months. There was a fourteen-month plan, sixty pages long, and honestly nobody on the floor believed a word of it. My first decision was to quietly put that plan in a drawer.

Instead, I picked one team — the inbound receiving crew — and one use case: scanning pallets on arrival instead of typing them in by hand. That's it. Nothing else. I told them, give me three days, and if it doesn't save you time, we stop.

By day three, receiving was twenty minutes faster per shift, and the supervisor was the one asking for more. That's the moment you want. Having proven that first benefit, I widened it to the next team, and then to picking. Each step earned its place before the next one started.

The old plan wanted everything live at once. That's exactly how you end up with expensive software nobody opens. I'd rather look unambitious for a quarter and have people actually using it by the end of the year.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What was the state of the WMS rollout when Emily took it over?
options: Stalled for months, with a plan nobody believed
items.why: "the WMS rollout had been stalled for months… nobody on the floor believed a word of it."

items.q: Which single use case did Emily start with?
options: Scanning pallets on arrival instead of typing them in
items.why: "one use case: scanning pallets on arrival instead of typing them in by hand."

items.q: What happened by day three?
options: The system crashed and had to be reset
Receiving was twenty minutes faster and the supervisor asked for more
The team asked to return to the old method
items.why: "By day three, receiving was twenty minutes faster per shift, and the supervisor was the one asking for more."

items.q: Why did Emily put the original fourteen-month plan "in a drawer"?
options: The vendor told her to ignore it
It was too expensive to follow
It focused only on the receiving crew
She believed doing everything at once would fail, as it had before
items.why: Inferência: ela prefere um começo pequeno; o plano queria tudo ao vivo de uma vez, "how you end up with expensive software nobody opens."

items.q: What does Emily mean by "Each step earned its place before the next one started"?
options: Each team paid for its own software
The steps happened in a random order
Every stage had to prove a benefit before the rollout widened
The plan was followed exactly as written
items.why: Inferência: ela só expande depois que a etapa anterior mostra valor e ganha confiança — adoção antes de escala.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The system was installed on time, but real adoption took another six months." Adoption here means…
options: the point at which the team actually uses it in their work
items.why: Adoption = adoção: quando a equipe de fato passa a usar a ferramenta no dia a dia.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We proved the idea with a single ___ — scanning pallets — before touching anything else."
items.why: Use case = caso de uso: um exemplo específico e concreto de aplicação.

items.q: "The rollout widened region by region over the year." A rollout is…
options: the gradual deployment of a system across an organisation
items.why: Rollout = implementação: colocar o sistema em uso de forma progressiva.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Once scanning became a daily ___, people stopped thinking of it as extra work."
items.why: Habit = hábito: algo que a equipe passa a fazer automaticamente.

items.q: "From the outside the pilot looked unambitious, yet it transformed the operation." Unambitious means…
items.why: Unambitious = sem ambição aparente: parece modesto por fora, mesmo tendo grande impacto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em projetos de implementação de tecnologia. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We are ready to roll out the WMS to the picking team next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, colocar em produção.

items.q: "The operations director still has to sign off on the pilot budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "A couple of supervisors pushed back on the new scanning process at first." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to log every pallet, but they never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out consistently
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim, cumprir de forma consistente o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A three-day quick win did more to move the needle on adoption than a year of memos." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir um efeito perceptível e mensurável.
